Marker Styling

Source: vignettes/articles/r-docs/marker-style.Rmd
marker-style.Rmd

Add Marker Border

In order to make markers distinct, you can add a border to the markers. This can be achieved by passing a go_scatter_marker_line() as the line of the marker, for example marker = go_scatter_marker(..., line = go_scatter_marker_line(...)).

library(plotly.core)

x <- runif(500, min = 3, max = 6)
y <- runif(500, min = 3, max = 6)

fig <- go_figure() |>
  add_scatter(
    mode = "markers",
    x = x,
    y = y,
    marker = go_scatter_marker(
      color = "rgb(17, 157, 255)",
      size = 20,
      line = go_scatter_marker_line(
        color = "rgb(231, 99, 250)",
        width = 2
      )
    ),
    showlegend = FALSE
  ) |>
  add_scatter(
    mode = "markers",
    x = c(2),
    y = c(4.5),
    marker = go_scatter_marker(
      color = "rgb(17, 157, 255)",
      size = 120,
      line = go_scatter_marker_line(
        color = "rgb(231, 99, 250)",
        width = 12
      )
    ),
    showlegend = FALSE
  )

fig

Fully Opaque

Fully opaque, the default setting, is useful for non-overlapping markers. When many points overlap it can be hard to observe density.

library(plotly.core)

x <- runif(500, min = 3, max = 6)
y <- runif(500, min = 3, max = 6)

fig <- go_figure() |>
  add_scatter(
    mode = "markers",
    x = x,
    y = y,
    marker = go_scatter_marker(
      color = "rgb(17, 157, 255)",
      size = 20,
      line = go_scatter_marker_line(
        color = "rgb(231, 99, 250)",
        width = 2
      )
    ),
    showlegend = FALSE
  ) |>
  add_scatter(
    mode = "markers",
    x = c(2, 2),
    y = c(4.25, 4.75),
    marker = go_scatter_marker(
      color = "rgb(17, 157, 255)",
      size = 120,
      line = go_scatter_marker_line(
        color = "rgb(231, 99, 250)",
        width = 12
      )
    ),
    showlegend = FALSE
  )

fig

Opacity

Setting opacity outside the marker will set the opacity of the trace. Thus, it will allow greater visbility of additional traces but like fully opaque it is hard to distinguish density.

library(plotly.core)

x <- runif(500, min = 3, max = 6)
y <- runif(500, min = 3, max = 4.5)
x2 <- runif(500, min = 3, max = 6)
y2 <- runif(500, min = 4.5, max = 6)

fig <- go_figure() |>
  add_scatter(
    mode = "markers",
    x = x,
    y = y,
    opacity = 0.5,
    marker = go_scatter_marker(
      color = "rgb(17, 157, 255)",
      size = 20,
      line = go_scatter_marker_line(
        color = "rgb(231, 99, 250)",
        width = 2
      )
    ),
    name = "Opacity 0.5"
  ) |>
  add_scatter(
    mode = "markers",
    x = x2,
    y = y2,
    marker = go_scatter_marker(
      color = "rgb(17, 157, 255)",
      size = 20,
      line = go_scatter_marker_line(
        color = "rgb(231, 99, 250)",
        width = 2
      )
    ),
    name = "Opacity 1.0"
  ) |>
  add_scatter(
    mode = "markers",
    x = c(2, 2),
    y = c(4.25, 4.75),
    opacity = 0.5,
    marker = go_scatter_marker(
      color = "rgb(17, 157, 255)",
      size = 120,
      line = go_scatter_marker_line(
        color = "rgb(231, 99, 250)",
        width = 12
      )
    ),
    showlegend = FALSE
  )

Marker Opacity

To maximise visibility of density, it is recommended to set the opacity inside the marker marker = go_scatter_marker(opacity = 0.5). If mulitple traces exist with high density, consider using marker opacity in conjunction with trace opacity.

library(plotly.core)

x <- runif(500, min = 3, max = 6)
y <- runif(500, min = 3, max = 6)

fig <- go_figure() |>
  add_scatter(
    mode = "markers",
    x = x,
    y = y,
    marker = go_scatter_marker(
      color = "rgb(17, 157, 255)",
      size = 20,
      opacity = 0.5,
      line = go_scatter_marker_line(
        color = "rgb(231, 99, 250)",
        width = 2
      )
    ),
    showlegend = FALSE
  ) |>
  add_scatter(
    mode = "markers",
    x = c(2, 2),
    y = c(4.25, 4.75),
    marker = go_scatter_marker(
      color = "rgb(17, 157, 255)",
      size = 120,
      opacity = 0.5,
      line = go_scatter_marker_line(
        color = "rgb(231, 99, 250)",
        width = 12
      )
    ),
    showlegend = FALSE
  )

Color Opacity

To maximise visibility of each point, set the color opacity by using alpha: marker = go_scatter_marker(color = "rgba(0,0,0,0.5)"). Here, the marker line will remain opaque.

library(plotly.core)

x <- runif(500, min = 3, max = 6)
y <- runif(500, min = 3, max = 6)

fig <- go_figure() |>
  add_scatter(
    mode = "markers",
    x = x,
    y = y,
    marker = go_scatter_marker(
      color = "rgba(17, 157, 255, 0.5)",
      size = 20,
      line = go_scatter_marker_line(
        color = "rgb(231, 99, 250)",
        width = 2
      )
    ),
    showlegend = FALSE
  ) |>
  add_scatter(
    mode = "markers",
    x = c(2, 2),
    y = c(4.25, 4.75),
    marker = go_scatter_marker(
      color = "rgba(17, 157, 255, 0.5)",
      size = 120,
      line = go_scatter_marker_line(
        color = "rgb(231, 99, 250)",
        width = 12
      )
    ),
    showlegend = FALSE
  )
